statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to the lower part of the low band because the reopened Globex session has now held a 29,490.00 to 29,522.50 range for roughly 75 minutes with the September contract 0.07 percent below its reference and no gap, while Stress stays elevated on Brent near 91 dollars, a 4.758 percent 10-year yield and roughly 62 percent implied odds of a September rate increase.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with a two-sided regime in which mean reversion is functioning. The reopened Globex session has traded 29,490.00 to 29,522.50 with the September E-mini Nasdaq-100 contract last at 29,493.25, down 19.75 points or 0.07 percent, a 32-point band across roughly 75 minutes with no opening gap and no chain of shallow pullbacks. Crude has been equally contained overnight, with WTI in an 86.13 to 86.49 range around 86.33 dollars, so the Hormuz premium priced during the cash session has not extended. The August month-end cash session closed at 29,456.97, up 0.08 percent, after traversing its full 29,304.49 to 29,483.90 range in both directions with repeatedly successful retracements. Cross-asset signals continue to conflict rather than align: the long end steepened with the 10-year at 4.758 percent against an effectively unchanged 2-year, the Dow fell 0.70 percent against a flat Nasdaq-100, megacap performance split sharply, semiconductors closed broadly higher, and VIX finished at 14.92 near the low of its 14.86 to 15.48 range. No further Middle East escalation has been reported since Iran's retaliation was described as intercepted with no impacts at United States bases. The identified conditional risks are an overnight Strait of Hormuz headline into thin Asian liquidity and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS releases at 14:00 UTC on 1 September, the only forecast hour mapped to WATCH.
headline: Globex holds a 32-point band with no gap after the Nasdaq-100 closes August at 29,456.97, while Brent near 91 dollars, a 4.758 percent 10-year and hawkish September repricing keep Stress elevated
body: The overnight tape is the central current observation. CME equity index futures reopened at 22:00 UTC after the daily maintenance halt, and roughly 75 minutes into the session the September E-mini Nasdaq-100 contract has held a 29,490.00 to 29,522.50 range and was last at 29,493.25, down 19.75 points or 0.07 percent from the 29,513 reference, with no opening gap. A 32-point band, about 0.11 percent wide, contains no directional impulse, no chain of shallow pullbacks and no repeated extension after failed retracements, so the pathological no-retracement path that would overwhelm a mean-reversion approach is absent from live evidence. Price sitting near the lower edge of that band is a drift of a few points, not directional efficiency. Crude has been similarly contained since the reopen: WTI has traded 86.13 to 86.49 and was last near 86.33 dollars, up 0.66 percent on the new session, which means the Hormuz risk premium repriced during the cash session has held rather than extended. The preceding cash session closed the August month-end at 29,456.97, up 23.54 points or 0.08 percent, after opening at 29,404.29 and traversing a 29,304.49 to 29,483.90 range in both directions with deep and repeatedly successful retracements. The broader tape was weaker and split: the Dow fell 374.09 points or 0.70 percent to 53,185.90, the S&P 500 fell 0.33 percent to 7,686.14 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.12 percent to 26,370.89, yet all three booked August gains, with the Nasdaq up more than 3 percent and the Dow completing a fifth consecutive monthly advance. Energy remains the dominant macro channel. WTI settled around 86.22 dollars, up 2.83 percent, and Brent around 90.79 dollars, up 2.71 percent, after United States forces struck two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guard responded with ballistic missiles against the King Hussein and Al Azraq air bases in Jordan and drones toward a United States-linked facility in the United Arab Emirates. Jordan's armed forces reported intercepting eight missiles before they posed a threat, a United States official stated there were no impacts at United States bases, and the Emirati defence ministry denied that Al Minhad itself was struck. That combination of an intercepted retaliation and de-escalatory framing materially limits the geopolitical discontinuity premium relative to an open-ended escalation, and no further escalation has been reported in the hours since. Rates repriced hawkishly along the long end. The 10-year yield rose 3.8 basis points to 4.758 percent within a 4.726 to 4.768 range while the 2-year was effectively unchanged near 4.354 percent, a steepening consistent with an oil-driven inflation impulse rather than a policy-path shock. Implied odds of a September rate increase are near 62 percent, up from roughly 40 percent a week earlier, following the Federal Reserve chair's Jackson Hole remark that inflation was running too hot. Volatility did not confirm the risk-off narrative: VIX closed at 14.92, up 3.40 percent, but finished near the low of its 14.86 to 15.48 range. Internals were split rather than aligned. Megacap performance dispersed sharply, with Tesla up about 5.5 percent and Nvidia up about 1.5 percent after announcing a 3.5 billion dollar convertible-bond investment in MediaTek, against Amazon down about 2.5 percent after the Federal Trade Commission and more than 20 states sued the company over advertising auction pricing, alongside declines in Alphabet and Microsoft. Semiconductors were broadly positive. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and raise Stress; they do not establish the persistent directional efficiency that Tail measures. Shared cross-asset context from the repository Finviz collector was older than its 90-minute freshness bound at this assessment, so it was not relied on and the assessment rests on directly verified primary sources. Confidence is held at 88 because live futures, cash-index, volatility, yield, crude and calendar evidence were all obtained directly, and the geopolitical sequence was verified against reporting rather than inferred. Tail is set to 9. Stress is set to 50 on the standing energy and long-end yield backdrop plus the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS releases at 14:00 UTC on 1 September, which is the only forecast hour mapped to WATCH and anchors a narrow declared danger window from 13:45 to 15:00 UTC. The dominant mode is mixed.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours run from the late Sunday Globex session through the August month-end United States cash close, the maintenance halt and the first hour of the reopened session. Published Tail opened at 14, peaked at 15 in the 00:00 UTC Asian repricing of the Larak Island strike, eased steadily to a 5 trough through the European morning, spiked to 17 at 09:00 UTC on the crude-led inflation impulse, then decayed and held a narrow 9 to 13 band across the entire United States session. Stress traced a wider arc from 36 at the European trough to a 55 peak in the United States afternoon before easing to 51 at the halt. Every one of the 24 slots is available, and every slot mapped to EA_ON and green, so no hour of the period reached even the WATCH threshold. Confidence held between 84 and 88 throughout. The shape of the series is the important part: two separate impulse spikes both decayed within one to two hours rather than compounding, which is the signature of a regime where retracements keep completing.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from the reopened Globex session through the Asian and European sessions and into the first September United States afternoon and close. Conditional Tail starts at 9 on the observed orderly reopen, rises to 12 at the 00:00 UTC Tokyo open as the highest overnight reading, eases to a 9 trough across the Asian close and the Asia-to-Europe handover, firms to 12 in the 09:00 UTC hour that carried the prior session's Tail peak, and rises to a conditional peak of 21 in the 14:00 UTC hour on 1 September when ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS Job Openings release simultaneously 30 minutes after the cash open. That single hour is the only one mapped to WATCH; every other hour maps to EA_ON. Tail then decays through the afternoon to 11 by the cash close and to a 24-hour low of 9 during the 21:00 UTC maintenance halt, before returning to 10 at the next Globex reopen. Stress follows the same shape between 47 and 58, and Confidence declines from 88 to 84 with distance from the assessment cutoff. Every forecast beyond the current clock-hour is a conditional scenario weight, not an assertion that any future price structure has already been observed.
